ann.l: Large hyperplastic prostate glands with characteristic papillary infoldings into the lumen. These glands are lined by a pseudostratified columnar epithelium with a pale secretory layer, representing epithelial overgrowth in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

A central hyperplastic nodule composed of crowded, smaller, closely packed glandular acini. Hyperplasia in BPH is characteristically nodular and originates predominantly within the periurethral transition zone.

Broad bands of pink fibromuscular stroma separating the hyperplastic glandular elements. BPH involves proliferation of both glandular epithelium and stromal smooth muscle/fibroblasts; alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists target this smooth muscle to reduce urethral resistance.

findings: Dilated glands with infoldings: large glands with wavy, papillary infoldings lie at the upper right, right and left edges, and they are lined by a tall, pale secretory layer. This is the glandular overgrowth of hyperplasia.

Glandular nodule: at the center a rounded cluster of smaller, closely grouped glands is surrounded by larger dilated glands, so gland size changes in an orderly way. This nodular pattern is typical of hyperplasia.

Expanded stroma: broad bands of pink fibromuscular stroma separate the glands across the field, because smooth muscle and stroma multiply as well as the glands. Alpha-1 blockers relax this smooth muscle.
